screening_decisions.reason: RCT comparing LMWH (nadroparin) to placebo in ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy for primary VTE prophylaxis. Meets all selection criteria.

While this is an RCT comparing LMWH to no anticoagulant in SCLC patients receiving chemotherapy, the primary objective was to assess improvement in clinical outcomes/survival rather than VTE prophylaxis. The study focused on antineoplastic effects of anticoagulants.

RCT evaluating warfarin addition to chemotherapy in SCLC, but primary outcomes were tumor response rates and survival, not VTE prevention. Study focused on potential antineoplastic effects of anticoagulation.
RCT comparing enoxaparin to control in SCLC, but primary outcome was overall survival, not VTE prevention. Supraprophylactic dose used to test survival benefit rather than VTE prophylaxis efficacy.
Phase II trial with three dalteparin dose groups but no control group (no anticoagulant arm). Cannot assess efficacy of thromboprophylaxis without comparison to no prophylaxis.
Pediatric population (children and adolescents with ALL), not adult ambulatory cancer patients. Also compares three anticoagulant interventions without a no-prophylaxis control.

Two double-blind RCTs (TOPIC-1 and TOPIC-2) comparing LMWH (certoparin) to placebo in ambulatory patients with metastatic breast or stage III/IV lung cancer for primary VTE prophylaxis. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing dalteparin to placebo in advanced cancer, but primary aim was to assess survival at 1 year, not VTE prevention. Study focused on potential antineoplastic effects of LMWH.

RCT comparing dalteparin to observation (no prophylaxis) in ambulatory cancer patients at high risk for VTE starting new systemic regimen. Primary endpoint was VTE occurrence. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing nadroparin to placebo in advanced malignancy, but primary efficacy analysis was time to death (survival), not VTE prevention. Study focused on survival benefit of LMWH.

RCT comparing two anticoagulant strategies (aspirin vs LMWH enoxaparin) for VTE prophylaxis in patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma receiving lenalidomide-based therapy. Meets criteria for comparing two different anticoagulants.

RCT comparing subcutaneous heparin to no heparin in SCLC, but primary outcomes were complete response rates and survival, not VTE prevention. Study focused on antineoplastic effects of anticoagulation.
RCT comparing bemiparin addition to standard therapy in SCLC, but primary outcome was progression-free survival, not VTE prevention. Study focused on survival benefit of anticoagulation.
Double-blind RCT comparing very-low-dose warfarin to placebo in women receiving chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer. Primary outcome was thromboembolic events. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing oral anticoagulant (apixaban) to placebo in patients with metastatic cancer receiving chemotherapy for VTE prevention. Secondary outcome included VTE. Meets selection criteria.
Large RCT comparing LMWH to control in lung cancer, but primary outcome was 1-year survival, not VTE prevention. While VTE reduction was observed, the study was designed to test survival benefit.
RCT comparing dalteparin thromboprophylaxis to no prophylaxis in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer receiving chemotherapy. Primary endpoint was reduction of VTE. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT comparing warfarin to no warfarin in SCLC, but primary outcomes were response rates and survival, not VTE prevention. Study evaluated potential enhancement of chemotherapy response by anticoagulation.
Pediatric population (children with ALL), not adult ambulatory cancer patients. Also, L-asparaginase-induced thrombosis prevention differs from general chemotherapy-associated VTE prophylaxis.

RCT comparing three anticoagulant strategies (aspirin, warfarin, LMWH) for VTE prophylaxis in patients with multiple myeloma receiving thalidomide-based regimens. Meets criteria for comparing different anticoagulants.
Randomised controlled trial comparing enoxaparin to observation in ambulatory pancreatic cancer patients receiving first-line chemotherapy for primary VTE prophylaxis. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomised placebo-controlled trial comparing dalteparin to placebo for VTE prophylaxis in patients with malignant glioma. Meets criteria for RCT comparing anticoagulant to placebo in cancer patients.

Randomised controlled trial comparing LMWH to standard care/placebo in advanced cancer patients. Although primarily designed for survival, it reports VTE rates and meets criteria for RCT comparing anticoagulant to control.
Randomised open-label trial comparing nadroparin to no treatment in patients with advanced lung, prostate, or pancreatic cancer. Reports VTE and bleeding outcomes. Meets criteria.

Randomised controlled trial comparing warfarin to control in small cell lung cancer patients receiving chemotherapy and radiation. Meets criteria for RCT comparing anticoagulant to control in cancer patients.
Randomised phase II trial comparing enoxaparin to observation in advanced cancer patients with elevated TFMP for VTE prophylaxis. Meets selection criteria.
Double-blind randomised trial comparing semuloparin to placebo in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy for VTE prophylaxis. Perfectly matches selection criteria.
Randomised placebo-controlled trial comparing apixaban to placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy for VTE prophylaxis. Meets all criteria.
Double-blind randomised trial comparing rivaroxaban to placebo in high-risk ambulatory cancer patients for VTE prophylaxis. Meets all criteria.
Reports further results of the FRAGMATIC trial, which is a known randomised controlled trial of fondaparinux versus placebo for VTE prophylaxis in lung cancer patients. Meets criteria.

Randomised phase III trial comparing tinzaparin to no treatment in resected NSCLC patients (subset receiving adjuvant chemotherapy). Reports VTE/recurrence outcomes. Meets criteria for RCT comparing anticoagulant to control.
Phase 2 clinical trial where aspirin was added mid-study, generating non-randomized cohort groups for comparison. Does not meet the randomised controlled trial design requirement.
Compares vena cava filter placement to conservative therapy but does not describe randomisation; appears to be an observational or non-randomised comparative study. Excluded based on study design.
Randomised phase 3 trial comparing nadroparin to control in patients with resected NSCLC receiving adjuvant chemotherapy. Meets criteria for RCT comparing anticoagulant to control.

Subgroup analysis of a randomised controlled trial comparing certoparin to UFH in acutely ill patients, including a cancer subgroup. Compares two different anticoagulants and reports VTE outcomes in cancer patients.

Randomised trial of intermittent pneumatic compression for postoperative DVT prophylaxis. The population consists of postoperative patients, not ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy. Excluded based on population/setting.
Explicitly described as an observational study comparing LMWH prophylaxis to no prophylaxis in multiple myeloma patients. Does not meet the RCT design requirement.
Prospective cohort study comparing combined LMWH/antithrombin to antithrombin alone in children with ALL using a non-contemporaneous control group. Not a randomised trial.
Descriptive report of three series of multiple myeloma patients receiving aspirin prophylaxis. Lacks randomised controlled trial design.
Economic evaluation based on data from a previous trial, not a primary clinical RCT reporting efficacy and safety outcomes for VTE prophylaxis. Excluded based on study type.

This study focuses on transcutaneous electrostimulation for pain management in patients with knee osteoarthritis. The population (osteoarthritis patients) is completely unrelated to the review's target population (ambulatory cancer patients receiving chemotherapy). The intervention (electrostimulation for pain) is not an anticoagulant or mechanical VTE prophylaxis. This study does not meet any of the selection criteria regarding population, intervention, or study focus.

This is an observational cohort study using Danish registry data to assess prognosis and survival of cancer patients diagnosed with or after VTE. It is NOT a randomised controlled trial. The study does not evaluate primary thromboprophylaxis interventions; rather, it examines outcomes (survival, metastasis rates) in patients who already have VTE. No comparison of anticoagulants or prophylaxis strategies is made. This study fails to meet the selection criteria for study design (not an RCT) and does not address the review objective of assessing efficacy/safety of primary prophylaxis.

This study describes the development of a modified Khorana risk assessment score (the Protecht score) for predicting VTE risk in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy. While the topic is related to VTE in cancer patients on chemotherapy, this paper is about risk score development/validation, NOT a randomised controlled trial comparing anticoagulant interventions. Although it references the PROTECT study (NCT 00951574) which tested nadroparin prophylaxis, this publication itself does not present RCT data comparing anticoagulants. It fails to meet the selection criteria requiring RCTs comparing anticoagulants or prophylaxis interventions.
